title: Critical Power Operations
summary: Interpret a simulated power transition and identify what operations teams monitor.
objectives: Describe the sequence from utility loss through backup stabilization in a simulation.
Identify safe operational questions during a power event without performing electrical service.

vocab.def: Equipment or service that must remain supported.
A change from one power source or state to another.
Reach a steady, monitored operating condition.

sections.heading: A power path has stages
sections.body: A conceptual path is utility input, facility distribution, UPS, generator, rack, and server. Operations teams monitor state changes and alarms across that path.

sections.heading: Read the scenario
sections.body: In a simulation, utility power is lost, the UPS supports the load, the generator starts, and the system stabilizes. Students record timestamps and identify what should be verified.

sections.heading: Electrical service is out of scope
sections.body: Do not open panels, service UPS units or generators, measure mains voltage, or work on energized power supplies. Escalate safety and equipment work to qualified professionals.

practice.prompt: Sequence synthetic power-event cards and list two values or statuses an operator would monitor during the transition.

quiz.question: What is the safe student role during a simulated power event?
options: Interpret the provided evidence and identify when to escalate
quiz.answer: Interpret the provided evidence and identify when to escalate

lab.objective: Analyze a synthetic power transition and complete an operational observation record.
